question_text:
The heights of a random sample of trees in an apple orchard are summarised in the table alongside.

| Height ($h\text{ m}$) | Frequency |
| :--- | :--- |
| $7 \leqslant h < 8$ | 8 |
| $8 \leqslant h < 9$ | 59 |
| $9 \leqslant h < 10$ | 74 |
| $10 \leqslant h < 11$ | 22 |
| $11 \leqslant h < 12$ | 1 |

subparts.stem: Construct a cumulative frequency graph for the data.

mark_breakdown.desc: Plotting points at upper class boundaries and drawing an S-shaped cumulative frequency curve

subparts.solution:
Cumulative frequency column values:
- $7 < h \le 8$: $8$
- $8 < h \le 9$: $8 + 59 = 67$
- $9 < h \le 10$: $67 + 74 = 141$
- $10 < h \le 11$: $141 + 22 = 163$
- $11 < h \le 12$: $163 + 1 = 164$
Plot the cumulative frequency at the upper class boundary of each interval: $(7, 0)$, $(8, 8)$, $(9, 67)$, $(10, 141)$, $(11, 163)$, $(12, 164)$ and join with a smooth curve.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Cumulative frequency is plotted against the upper class boundary of each group, starting from zero at the lower boundary of the first group.
step_by_step: Sum the frequencies progressively to get cumulative totals: 8, 67, 141, 163, 164.
Plot points $(h, \text{cf})$ at the upper boundaries: $(8, 8), (9, 67), (10, 141), (11, 163), (12, 164)$ starting from $(7,0)$.
Draw a smooth ogive connecting these points.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Plotting cumulative frequencies at midpoints instead of upper class boundaries.

mark_breakdown.desc: Reading median height from the cumulative frequency curve

subparts.solution:
The median is the 50th percentile.
$$50\% \text{ of } 164 = 82$$
Find 82 on the cumulative frequency axis and read across to the curve and down to the horizontal axis:
$$\text{median} \approx 9.1\text{ m}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The median corresponds to $0.50 \times N$ on the vertical cumulative frequency axis.
step_by_step: Move horizontally to intersect the curve, then read vertically down to the height axis to find $\approx 9.1\text{ m}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Reading from the midpoint of the height axis rather than the cumulative frequency axis.

subparts.solution:
$Q_1$ is the 25th percentile. $25\% \text{ of } 164 = 41$.
From the graph, $Q_1 \approx 8.7\text{ m}$.
$Q_3$ is the 75th percentile. $75\% \text{ of } 164 = 123$.
From the graph, $Q_3 \approx 9.6\text{ m}$.
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 \approx 9.6 - 8.7 = 0.9\text{ m}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The interquartile range is $Q_3 - Q_1$, obtained by finding the heights corresponding to $0.25N$ and $0.75N$ on the cumulative frequency curve.
step_by_step: Find cumulative frequency for $Q_1$: $0.25 \times 164 = 41$, giving height $\approx 8.7\text{ m}$.
Find cumulative frequency for $Q_3$: $0.75 \times 164 = 123$, giving height $\approx 9.6\text{ m}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Misreading the graph values or calculating $123 - 41$ instead of heights.

subparts.stem: Estimate the 90th percentile. Interpret your answer.

mark_breakdown.desc: Reading corresponding height of approximately 10.2 m and providing interpretation

subparts.solution:
$$90\% \text{ of } 164 = 147.6$$
Locate cumulative frequency 147.6 on the vertical axis and find the corresponding height.
The 90th percentile is $\approx 10.2\text{ m}$, which means that $90\%$ of trees are shorter than about $10.2\text{ m}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The $k$th percentile is the value below which $k\%$ of the observations fall.
step_by_step: Locate 147.6 on the cumulative frequency axis.
Trace across to the curve and read down to obtain $\approx 10.2\text{ m}$.
Interpret: 90% of trees have a height of 10.2 m or less.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Reading from height = 9.0 instead of calculating 90% of the total frequency.
